paragraphs.source_en: In the third year of Tenshō, spring had barely touched Kōfu. Mountain ranges stretched endlessly on every side; lingering snow showed faintly in the hollows, and the courtyard was thick with frost columns. Takeda Katsuyori trod across the frost and snow, inspecting the officers and men assembled inside and outside the castle. To his eyes, this was a powerful, well-mounted force upon which he could rely completely.

paragraphs.source_en: Unlike the road to Suruga and Tōtōmi, this route had the Kiso Mountains immediately to the army’s right. paragraphs.source_en: No matter where the enemy deployed from, his own side was now united in purpose, and Katsuyori was pleased.
